lesson_title: The Drawings Trap and the Tin That Tells the Truth
hook_text: The owner paid herself R2 500. Expense? Wrong — and the mistake changes the whole year's profit.
clip_script: Ask the question that sorts every payment: what did the STORE get for this money? For the R9 500 to Coastal Wholesalers — the store got stock; the shelves are fuller. For wages — the store got a week of work. For rent — a month under a roof. And for the R2 500 to Lindi? The store got... nothing. The OWNER got something — perfectly allowed; it is her business — but it is not a cost of running the store. It is the owner dipping into her own stake: drawings.
visual_style: Payments sliding into three glowing bins — ASSET, EXPENSE, DRAWINGS — with the R2 500 hovering dramatically before dropping into the right one.
pacing: Rapid-fire sorting of easy payments, long pause on the trap, decisive landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master the CPJ and the self-auditing petty cash tin.
